transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-11-20 Time: 3:00 PM PT Duration: 58 minutes Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Calyx CTO), Liam (Lead ML), Sofia (DevOps), Tom (SRE)

00:00 Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time today. quick agenda: a short intro, parity map overview for OpenAI/Anthropic/Together, console quick tour (Optimize + rollout), and time for Q&A and next steps.
00:22 Priya (Calyx): thanks Maya, yeah we are trying to consolidate a bunch of endpoints — currently OpenAI for chat, Anthropc — sorry Anthropic for longform, and Together for our embedded scoring. main goals: reduce cost, keep latency under 250ms p50 for chat, and not regress quality.
00:48 Maya (Redwood): great, that's super common. Ethan and I will walk through how Redwood maps model calls, and then show the console suggestions for batching/quantization. quick question — is data residency a hard constraint?
01:05 Priya (Calyx): we need EU residency for PII flows. some teams can use hosted but others will need a VPC private deployment.
01:16 Ethan (Redwood SE): noted. Redwood has hosted, dedicated, and private with KMS/HSM integrations; we can show the private plane option later.
01:30 Liam (Customer): can you explain how function calling maps? we rely heavily on OpenAI-style function calling and structured outputs.
01:44 Maya: yeah we'll demo that. Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured outputs; there are minor differences in the request/response envelope but we provide client-side helpers and SDK shims to keep your code intact — usually a ~1-2 line change.
02:05 Ethan: jumping into parity mapping — high level: map OpenAI chat to Redwood chat endpoints, keep system/user roles, convert model names to Redwood-verified variants. Anthropic-style single-turn longform maps to appropriate Redwood long-context models. Together… their api object names are different so we provide a translate layer.
02:28 Speaker 1 (Customer - unclear): um, so does that mean we lose any special sampling or safety config?
02:34 Ethan: good question. Redwood surfaces the same sampling controls (temperature, top_p) and adds recommendations via Optimize; for safety we have guardrails and can integrate your filters. some safety configs may need small prompt adjustments.
03:10 Maya: quick console demo — opening the Console -> Models -> Parity tab (screen link shared: https://console.redwood.ai/playbooks/migration). note: link is provisional, internal demo view.
03:30 Ethan: here you can upload an existing OpenAI/Together prompt set, the system will run a token-level diff and show model equivalence, plus suggested quantization and batch sizes. this is where Optimize kicks in with cost/latency tradeoff suggestions.
03:52 Priya: seen a few screenshots in the deck, can you show how metrics align — p50/p95 and token spend?
04:08 Ethan: yep. the console shows token cost estimate per-run, p50/p95 latency from our verified profiles, and an estimated per-million-token spend. these are heuristics but we've validated with similar stacks.
04:35 Tom (SRE): curious about KV cache mention — how does the cache behave across private deployments? we need to preserve session state but not leak across customers.
04:50 Ethan: probably misheard — KV cache (key-value cache). Redwood supports tenant-isolated KV caches; in private deployments you can opt for local-only caches or a shared in-VPC cache with strict RBAC. there may be a small warm-up penalty on first session.
05:12 Sofia: what about auto-batching? some peaks are bursty and we care about latency tails.
05:22 Ethan: auto-batching is adaptive — you can set a latency SLO and Redwood will batch up to the SLO while honoring p50 targets; there's also a dedicated burst pool option for sustained throughput and sudden spikes (Reserved/Dedicated).
05:48 Priya: do you have data on quality regressions when quantizing? we have large instruction-following prompts.
06:02 Ethan: Optimize will run on your sample prompts and show per-prompt BLEU/ROUGE-style diffs and human-simulated scoring. quantization recommendations are per-model and per-workload; for instruction-following we often suggest fp16 or low-precision with careful evals.
06:28 Maya: sharing a parity spreadsheet now — example rows: source provider, endpoint, call shape, sample prompt, recommended Redwood model, required code changes, expected latency delta, expected cost delta.
06:44 Liam: about function calling again — do you keep function metadata in the response or is it extracted server-side?
06:52 Ethan: it's returned in a similar envelope. sometimes name fields are slightly different; our SDK normalizes that. in a few edge cases we add a shim that rewrites the function signature at the SDK layer.
07:10 Priya: security — SOC 2, SSO, SAML, audit logs — we need proof for procurement.
07:20 Maya: we are SOC 2 Type II, have SAML SSO, role-based access controls, and per-tenant audit trails. for private deployments we support your KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and on-prem HSMs) and can provide architecture diagrams.
07:38 Tom: any pen-test or external attestation?
07:42 Maya: we have third-party pentest reports; I'll include the summary in the follow-up.
07:50 Priya: excellent.
08:00 Ethan: going back to routing and fallbacks — Redwood can route by policy: latency-first, cost-first, or region-first. if a model variant is unavailable we can fallback to a compatible variant automatically. routing rules can be per-route.
08:22 Sofia: how deterministic is the fallback? we cannot have a sudden quality drop cause customer-facing errors.
08:30 Ethan: you can attach rollback policies and A/B tests. Canary deploys in the console let you route a percentage of traffic to the new model and monitor quality metrics; automatic rollback if the quality or latency regress beyond configured thresholds.
08:54 Priya: any vendor lock-in concerns with SDKs? we want to keep the option to switch again.
09:03 Maya: SDKs are shims — we prioritize keeping the same request shapes; we also provide an adapter layer so flipping providers is a small change. the parity spreadsheet documents exact delta-lines of code.
09:20 Liam: latency — 250ms p50 target for chat. can you run an eval on our prompt set and estimate needed instance types?
09:33 Ethan: yes — that is part of a pilot. we run load profiles, model selection, and show recommended instance families and batch configs. for 250ms p50 we often recommend low-latency instance families with optimized kernels.
09:50 Speaker 2 (background): mm-hmm
10:10 Maya: demoing Optimize -> Suggestions: for your chat workload Optimize suggests continuous batching enabled, soft prefix caching for repeated system prompts, and mixed-precision quantization for cost savings. each suggestion includes expected token savings and latency impact.
10:35 Liam: what about chronology and context length? we have threads up to 8k tokens sometimes.
10:44 Ethan: Redwood supports long-context models; we manage KV cache and memory to keep recency without re-encoding full history. there are config knobs and we can recommend truncated roll-up strategies to preserve cost/latency.
10:58 Priya: curious on pricing model during a pilot — do you charge host-level or per-token?
11:08 Maya: for hosted it's usage-based per-token. for Dedicated you can do commit-based reserved capacity plus overage. for Private it's license + infra. Pilot pricing often is a short-term blended rate — we'll include options in the pricing packet.
11:30 Sofia: network egress costs for private deployments?
11:36 Ethan: egress is your cloud bill; Redwood doesn't add egress, but we account for region routing to minimize cross-region traffic.
11:50 Priya: any gotchas migrating from Together's embeddings vs Redwood's embedding models?
11:58 Ethan: embeddings are often the easiest — the main differences are normalization and dimensionality. we provide migration tools that compute nearest-neighbor deltas and recommend retraining or reindex thresholds.
12:18 Maya: showing a sample parity diff for a Together endpoint — token count delta, suggested model variant, and estimated cost change.
12:36 Liam: are there any parts of the SDK that assume proprietary Together behavior?
12:42 Ethan: only a couple of helper endpoints; our adapter layer handles them. we flagged a minor function-call edge-case in the spreadsheet.
13:05 Priya: procurement timeline — we hope to decide within 4 weeks, pilot to start in early December.
13:15 Maya: that's doable; we'll aim to have the pilot plan and pricing by 11/22 and kickoff week of 11/30.
13:26 Tom: for the private deployment, how long to stand up?
13:32 Maya: typical private deployment spin-up is 2-4 weeks depending on networking approvals, KMS integration, and capacity provisioning. we provision a staging VPC first.
13:40 Sofia: what does observability look like? do we get token-level traces?
13:47 Ethan: yes — Console gives per-route token breakdown, latency percentiles, per-token cost estimates, and tracing hooks you can export to your APM.
14:05 Priya: show me how rollouts look in the console — can you demo an A/B?
14:12 Ethan: demoing console: Rollouts -> New -> choose baseline model -> new model -> percentage split -> metrics to monitor (latency, hallucination rate, cost). set a threshold for auto rollback.
14:40 Maya: quick Q from our side — which team owns SSO at Calyx?
14:45 Priya: that's Tom and Sofia.
14:50 Maya: perfect, we'll include SAML setup docs in the follow-up.
15:00 Ethan: last question: any compliance checklists we should preemptively send?
15:07 Priya: yes, procurement needs SOC 2, data flow diagrams, SLA, indemnification language.
15:15 Maya: we'll include all of that.
15:25 Maya: ok let's recap: Redwood will send parity spreadsheet, console recording, pricing options, SOC 2 and SSO docs. Calyx will share prompt sets, VPC diagram, and SLO targets. pilot kickoff targeted week of 11/30.
15:40 Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
15:45 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with the email. meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels were auto-assigned. occasional word errors (Anthropic spelled 'Anthopc' in the middle). References shared: parity spreadsheet (link sent), console demo recording (will be shared).
